convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom indicator 'XRVI' which is not a built-in MT5 indicator, plus external .mqh libraries (SmoothAlgorithms.mqh, TradeAlgorithms.mqh) for smoothing algorithms and trade execution logic.

derived_values.name: min_rates_total - minimum bars required before calculation
TimeShiftSec - chart period in seconds
derived_values.used_by: UpSignalTime and DnSignalTime for position open timing

other_exits: Opposite signal closes existing position: XRVI MAIN crossing below SIGNAL closes longs, crossing above closes shorts

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Negative MM values are treated as fixed lot size (0.1 lots), positive values are treated as deposit fraction for money management

custom_logic_notes: The crossover detection uses bars at SignalBar and SignalBar+1 indices: Value[1]>SigValue[1] checks the older bar direction, while Value[0]<=SigValue[0] confirms the crossover occurred at the SignalBar. SignalBar=1 means the signal is confirmed on the most recently closed bar. The Recount flag forces recalculation if CopyBuffer fails. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose are boolean permission gates that can independently disable each trading direction. GlobalVariableDel_ is called on deinit for cleanup.
python_conversion_notes: The XRVI custom indicator must be reimplemented in Python since it uses iCustom with custom smoothing methods (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh. The crossover logic is standard: MAIN_LINE crosses SIGNAL_LINE. Entry uses SignalBar=1 (previous closed bar) for signal confirmation. Position sizing has dual mode: negative MM = fixed lots, positive = deposit fraction. TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, LoadHistory, CIsNewBar) must be reimplemented. The smoothing algorithms (JJMA, JurX etc.) are non-trivial and will require careful porting from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh or finding Python equivalents.
